text_zh:
国仪量子登陆上交所科创板，
“量子精密测量第一股”诞生
8月11日，国仪量子技术（合肥）股份有限公司在上海证券交易所科创板挂牌上市。国仪公司成立于2016年，专注于量子精密测量与高端科学仪器的研发与产业化，是少数具备量子传感器全链条自主研发能力的企业，也是国内唯一具备电子顺磁共振波谱仪自主研发及生产能力的企业。公司核心产品涵盖量子钻石单自旋谱仪、电子顺磁共振波谱仪、扫描电镜等高端科学仪器。
来源：
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/-PKLOkulGaWJlYLpZ5zvmg
中国科学技术大学等
实现量子存储器间跨越
420
公里量子纠缠
本研究报道两个原子系综量子存储器在
420公里光纤上的纠缠。研究人员采用DLCZ方案生成远程纠缠，并将光子转换为电信S波段以利用超低损耗。通过全时远失谐锁定抑制高频噪声和间歇双波段锁定补偿低频漂移，稳定了光子相对相位。纠缠概率超过了直接分发的无中继信道容量，为超越城域规模的量子网络应用提供了测试平台。研究成果于8月11日发表于《Physical Review Letters》（物理评论快报）。
来源：
https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstra
ct/10.1103/ccd6-rf1s
犹他
州
州长启动量子倡议，加速量子技术发展

纽约州启动
6000
万美元区域量子技术商业化枢纽招标
8月12日，纽约州提供高达6000万美元的资金，用于建立多达四个区域中心，专注于量子技术商业化和支持初创企业。帝国州发展学院科学、技术与创新司（NYSTAR）预计每个枢纽将获得约1500万美元的补助，每个经济发展区仅选定一个枢纽。符合条件的非营利组织必须提出提供共享基础设施、支持技术开发和初创孵化，并将研究人员与行业合作伙伴连接起来的实体设施。

韩国发布未来增长动力七大
SEED
计划，涵盖
量子领域
8月12日,韩国政府正式公布“未来增长动力七大SEED计划”，将量子技术列为支撑国家未来发展的核心前沿领域。根据规划，韩国计划于2029年前研发出具备纠错能力的100量子比特处理器，并由本土企业主导开发涵盖芯片与软件的全栈式量子计算机。政府还计划依托半导体领域的技术优势，通过以大型半导体企业为中心的特殊目的公司（SPC）推进“K-量子代工”项目，建立量子芯片量产体系，并力争在10年内跻身全球量子制造能力第一梯队。此外，韩国将指定超广域量子集群，发掘与地方主力产业相结合的量子应用场景，同时构建量子安全体系。

# Weekly Report | Birth of "China's First Quantum Precision Measurement IPO": Guoyi Quantum Lists on STAR Market; USTC and Collaborators Achieve Quantum Entanglement Between Memory Nodes Across 420 km…

---

## Guoyi Quantum Lists on Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market — "First Quantum Precision Measurement IPO" Born

On August 11, Guoyi Quantum Technology (Hefei) Co., Ltd. (国仪量子技术（合肥）股份有限公司) officially listed on the STAR Market of the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Founded in 2016, the company focuses on the R&D and commercialization of quantum precision measurement and high-end scientific instrumentation. It is one of a small number of enterprises with full-chain in-house R&D capabilities for quantum sensors, and the only domestic enterprise with independent R&D and production capabilities for electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrometers. Its core products include quantum diamond single-spin spectrometers, EPR spectrometers, and scanning electron microscopes.

**Source:** https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/-PKLOkulGaWJlYLpZ5zvmg

## USTC and Collaborators Achieve Quantum Entanglement Between Quantum Memories Across 420 km

This study reports entanglement between two atomic-ensemble quantum memories over 420 km of optical fiber. The researchers employed the DLCZ (Duan–Lukin–Cirac–Zoller) scheme to generate remote entanglement and converted photons to the telecom S-band to exploit ultra-low loss. High-frequency noise was suppressed via full-time far-detuned locking, and low-frequency drift was compensated via intermittent dual-band locking, thereby stabilizing the relative photon phase. The entanglement rate exceeded the repeaterless channel capacity of direct transmission, providing a testbed for quantum network applications beyond metropolitan scale. The results were published in *Physical Review Letters* on August 11.

**Source:** https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/ccd6-rf1s

## Utah Governor Launches Quantum Initiative to Accelerate Quantum Technology Development

On August 10, Utah Governor Spencer Cox launched the Utah Quantum Initiative to accelerate quantum research, commercialization, workforce development, and advanced manufacturing across the state. The initiative establishes a Quantum Coordination Committee to coordinate efforts among the state government, universities, and industry, and to compete for private investment and federal quantum funding. Utah plans to leverage existing strengths in quantum sensing, photonics, semiconductors, high-performance computing, defense, and life sciences to develop its quantum technology sector.

**Source:** https://governor.utah.gov/press/gov-cox-launches-utah-quantum-initiative/

## New York State Launches $60 Million RFP for Regional Quantum Technology Commercialization Hubs

On August 12, New York State announced up to $60 million in funding to establish as many as four regional hubs focused on quantum technology commercialization and startup support. The New York State Foundation for Science, Technology and Innovation (NYSTAR) expects each hub to receive approximately $15 million in grants, with only one hub selected per economic development region. Eligible non-profit organizations must propose physical facilities that offer shared infrastructure, support technology development and startup incubation, and connect researchers with industry partners.

**Source:** https://www.governor.ny.gov/news/governor-hochul-announced-launch-selection-process-regional-quantum-technology

## South Korea Releases Seven Future Growth Engine SEED Plans, Including Quantum

On August 12, the South Korean government officially announced the "Seven Future Growth Engine SEED Plans," designating quantum technology as a core frontier domain underpinning the nation's future development. According to the plan, South Korea aims to develop a 100-qubit processor with error correction capabilities by 2029, with domestic enterprises taking the lead in developing full-stack quantum computers encompassing chips and software. The government also plans to leverage strengths in the semiconductor sector, advancing the "K-Quantum Foundry" project through special-purpose companies (SPCs) centered on large semiconductor firms to establish a quantum chip mass-production ecosystem, with the goal of joining the global top tier in quantum manufacturing capability within ten years. In addition, South Korea will designate ultra-wide quantum clusters, identify quantum application scenarios integrated with regional key industries, and build a quantum security framework.

**Source:** https://chinese.korea.net/NewsFocus/Sci-Tech/view?articleId=297801

(QCi) reported second-quarter revenue of $5.6 million, driven primarily by acquired businesses, while continuing to expand its quantum, photonics, and semiconductor operations. The company recorded an operating loss of $23 million and a total net loss of $1.2 million; its $1.3 billion in cash and investments generated approximately $13 million in interest and other income. ## Pasqal Demonstrates Neutral-Atom Quantum Computer Control via Photonic Chip

On August 10, Pasqal announced a demonstration using photonic integrated circuits developed in collaboration with Aeponyx to generate laser-based optical traps for trapping individual atoms in a neutral-atom quantum processor. The demonstration produced four optical traps from a single photonic chip, with atom lifetimes comparable to those of Pasqal's existing free-space optical systems. Pasqal aims to scale the integrated photonics approach to future fault-tolerant quantum processors hosting more than 10,000 atoms and 100 logical qubits.

## Eaton and Infleqtion Collaborate to Explore Quantum Computing for Grid Resilience

On August 10, Infleqtion was selected by Eaton to provide quantum computing capabilities for research aimed at enhancing U.S. electrical grid resilience, under a project funded by the Air Force Research Laboratory. On August 11, according to *The Quantum Insider*, the Havana-based Quantum Computing Open Lab (QCOL) is developing an open software platform designed to make quantum computing tools more accessible across different hardware and software systems. QCOL has built a fully functional browser-based prototype that integrates visual circuit design, code editing, educational tools, and support for multiple quantum programming frameworks. The early-stage team is assembling international developers through QWorld's QIntern 2026 program and is seeking to establish QCOL as a U.S. company.

**Source:** https://thequantuminsider.com/2026/08/11/cuba-based-team-builds-open-platform-aimed-at-making-quantum-computing-easier-to-use/

## PsiQuantum Appoints Atomico Founder Niklas Zennström to Board of Directors

On August 11, PsiQuantum appointed Niklas Zennström, founder and CEO of Atomico, to its board of directors as the company continues to develop its large-scale quantum computing platform. Zennström brings experience as a technology founder, investor, and board member, including co-founding Skype and leading Atomico's investments in technology companies. The appointment follows further leadership changes at PsiQuantum as it advances quantum computing programs in the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom.

**Source:** https://www.psiquantum.com/news-import/psiquantum-appoints-niklas-zennstrom-to-board-of-directors

## Yonsei University to Install IBM Nighthawk Quantum Processor for Research and Industrial Applications

On August 12, according to the Seoul Economic Daily, the Yonsei University Quantum Initiative plans to install IBM's Nighthawk quantum processor in November, making it reportedly the second Nighthawk-based quantum computing site after IBM Miami. The initiative will launch the Q-Bridge platform, designed to connect industrial users with quantum algorithms, data resources, and computing capacity. Yonsei is expanding its quantum research activities through drug discovery, hybrid quantum–classical computing projects, and collaborations with institutions including RIKEN and the University of Cambridge.

**Source:** https://en.sedaily.com/technology/2026/08/12/yonsei-to-build-worlds-second-nighthawk-quantum-computer

## BLOQ Quantum and Srirama Engineering College Partner to Advance Quantum Education in Andhra Pradesh

On August 12, BLOQ Quantum and Srirama Engineering College (Srirama College of Engineering) partnered to launch a quantum computing program focused on education, research, and skills development. The collaboration provides students and faculty with access to the BLOQ Quantum computing platform for learning quantum algorithms, programming, and research applications. The partnership will support joint research, technical training, publications, and industry–academia collaboration in quantum computing and related fields.
